site.name: Sangrur District, Punjab
site.note: Rice-wheat on the central Punjab plain, irrigated from a falling water table. Run on global inputs only - predicted soil, no yield series to check against - so every number here is the engine transferred, not validated.

soil.source: SoilGrids v2.0 250 m prediction, 200 cm described; hydrologic group from texture class

terrain.note: no DEM tile downloaded for this site, so the slope-length factor uses a placeholder of 0.25; the erosion figure here is indicative only

region.name: Indian Punjab
review_first: Transplanting and sowing dates. These are central-Punjab practice in round numbers; a two-week shift in the rice transplanting date changes seasonal water use materially, and the state's own date restrictions have moved over the period simulated.

Percolation under puddled paddy, held at 4 mm/day. This is the largest single assumption in the Punjab run and it depends on whether a plough pan has formed. Local measurement would change the rice water figure more than any other input.

The hydrologic group. SoilGrids has none, so it falls back to the texture class, which puts this point in group D. Punjab's alluvial soils are usually reported as lighter than that, and group D overstates monsoon runoff - which penalises the rainfed options against the ponded ones.
Nitrogen rates, entered as regional recommended doses rather than what this farmer applies. Punjab application is widely reported to exceed the recommendation for rice and wheat.
Yield response factors for pigeonpea, mungbean and sesame, which have no FAO-33 entry and use a pulse analogue of Ky = 0.9.
region.note: Rice-wheat over a falling water table. The same shape of problem as the Ogallala - a profitable monoculture mining a finite aquifer - which is why it is the transfer case worth running.

objectives.label: production (dry matter)
objectives.note: summed as dry matter, because marketed weight cannot be added across crops holding different amounts of water - 25 t/ha of potato is about 5 t/ha of dry matter. Becomes margin when local prices are supplied.

objectives.label: production in a bad year
objectives.note: tenth percentile across simulated years for THIS FIELD, including years it produces nothing. A farmer staggering the rotation across several fields sees a steadier farm-level income; compare with production for that view.

objectives.label: irrigation demand
objectives.note: at the field gate, including application losses; the binding constraint where groundwater is declining

objectives.label: soil carbon change
objectives.note: RothC over the simulated period, 0-23 cm

objectives.label: wind erosion exposure
objectives.note: ordinal, for comparing rotations at one site; not a mass flux

objectives.label: bare ground
objectives.note: the clearest single explanation behind carbon loss and erosion exposure
